claims.text: The reroute was not traffic-justified. The LTA record returned for Bedok Road — the recommended route — overlaps the trip window (valid 10:58 to 12:28 on 2026-08-09, trip 11:28–11:39) and reports advisory_type NONE: no incident, roadwork or closure, with speed bands 4–6 throughout, so the recommended road was running normally. POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify a reroute, so the counterparty's account of a long bus stop and traffic light cannot carry rows (a) to (c) of POL-RD-24, and the deviation through Jalan Bilal and Siglap Road was an unjustified departure from the app route.

The rider was never told of the deviation before or at the point of deviation, and never agreed to it. The chat log holds exactly two messages, both before the trip started at 11:28:02: the driver's 11:26:22 message about the Bedok Mall taxi stand and the rider's 11:26:52 'ok', which answers that message and nothing else. Nothing was sent at or after the 11:30:14 deviation point, when the car turned off New Upper Changi Road into Jalan Bilal; the trip record's in_app_calls list is empty and its messages-during-trip list is empty. POL-RD-21 requires the rider to be informed by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, and adds that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established — so on this record the notice obligation is simply failed and the rider's 'ok' cannot be stretched into agreement to a reroute he was never told about.

I concede the point that decides the money against the rider on distance, and I do not stretch it. On the platform's recorded distances — actual 5.2 km less recommended 4.6 km — the deviation is 0.60 km, which is under POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, and row (e) of POL-RD-24 allocates no refund for a not-justified deviation of 1 km or less. I do not ask the tribunal to re-measure on the GPS trace: POL-RD-22 excludes exactly that, because a sparse trace understates a route's length, and this one measures only 4.315 km from 23 fixes. So the rider's case cannot be met out of the deviation matrix, and I say so rather than overstate it.

The rider's $2.00 figure is not one the record supports, and the rider does not press it. The only measure of the excess POL-RD-24 provides is the excess distance fare on the policy formula — deviation 0.60 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd of 0.72, without surge — which the fare ledger's own derivation puts at 0.43 SGD, against 9.42 SGD charged and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. Even on the rider's own theory of the case, then, the contested 2.00 SGD exceeds anything this policy would return; what the rider actually complains of is being taken off Bedok Road with neither a justification nor a word of notice, and that is the finding I ask the tribunal to record on this trip.

I concede the point that decides the money against the rider on distance, and I do not stretch it. On the platform's recorded distances — actual 5.2 km less recommended 4.6 km — the deviation is 0.60 km, which is under POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, and row (e) of POL-RD-24 allocates no refund for a not-justified deviation of 1 km or less. I do not ask the tribunal to re-measure on the GPS trace: POL-RD-22 excludes exactly that, because a sparse trace understates a route's length, and this one measures only 4.315 km from 23 fixes. So the rider's case cannot be met out of the deviation matrix, and I say so rather than overstate it.

The rider's $2.00 figure is not one the record supports, and the rider does not press it. The only measure of the excess POL-RD-24 provides is the excess distance fare on the policy formula — deviation 0.60 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd of 0.72, without surge — which the fare ledger's own derivation puts at 0.43 SGD, against 9.42 SGD charged and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. Even on the rider's own theory of the case, then, the contested 2.00 SGD exceeds anything this policy would return; what the rider actually complains of is being taken off Bedok Road with neither a justification nor a word of notice, and that is the finding I ask the tribunal to record on this trip.

The deviation is measured under POL-RD-22 as the platform's recorded actual distance minus the recorded recommended distance — 5.2 km minus 4.6 km = 0.60 km — and POL-RD-22 fixes the tolerance at 1.0 km, so this reroute is within tolerance. The clause also directs that the sparse 23-fix GPS trace is not used to re-measure the distance, so nothing on the record displaces the recorded 0.60 km.

With a deviation of 0.60 km — 1.0 km or less — only rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24's refund matrix can apply, and both prescribe no refund as within tolerance. Row (e) applies even where the reroute is not traffic-justified, and row (c) even where the rider was not informed of it, so neither the traffic question nor the informing question changes the answer. No row of POL-RD-24 returns the contested difference on these distances, and the rider's claim for it back is not supported.

The driver's answer was that Bedok Road was slow, and the LTA advisory for the recommended Bedok Road segment indeed records type NONE, which POL-RD-23 does not accept as congestion, an incident or a closure. That does not assist the rider: POL-RD-24 row (e) gives no refund for a deviation of 1.0 km or less whether or not the reroute was traffic-justified, so even on the rider's best framing of the traffic point the answer is the same.

This is a case the AI may decide, not one to be held for a human. POL-RD-25 puts a 2 km ceiling on the deviation for an AI ruling and the deviation here is 0.60 km, well inside it; POL-GEN-22 makes the AI ruling final below 10.00 SGD and the rider contests 2.00 SGD. No limb of POL-RD-25 is engaged, so the fare should be settled now on this record.

The rider filed this dispute, and the fare stands charged with refund_issued_sgd at 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative: it leaves the present payment state standing. The driver therefore keeps the metered fare of 9.42 SGD and the rider's contested 2.00 SGD is not returned.

Nothing in POL-GEN-26 requires escalation on completeness. Every artifact in this case is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 — the trip record, the driver trace at 100% coverage with no gap exceeding 30 s, the chat log, the payments ledger, the LTA advisory — so each fact POL-RD-24 needs (both recorded distances, the trace showing which route was taken and when, and the traffic advisory) is established on the record.
